why: One knob moves: the teacher. ci-106 was recorded from search-4 on seeds 1, 5001 and 10001; this turn records from mixture-mean, the first set that beats search-4 head to head on unseen seeds (0.746 against search-4, 0.864 against Greedy, 0.998 against Random; journal, 2026-09-16), with everything else ci-106's: 5000 matches, the spaced seeds, lambda 0.9, the ADR 0048 baseline, explore 0.2. The baseline opponent stays search-4 on purpose: it is the bar every turn since 2026-09-15 has been read against and the champion ci-69 is a clone of it, so the clone rows stay comparable turn to turn; the clone against its own teacher is what the champion comparison and a later evaluate-policy can say. The question: a clone is capped by what it imitates, and every clone of search-4 read at parity with search-4 (ci-106: 0.5513, 0.6175, 0.5625). Does a clone of a teacher that beats search-4 by 25 points beat search-4? Expectations written before the run: clone against Greedy between the clone of search-4 (0.74 to 0.80) and the teacher itself (0.86); clone against search-4 above one half on every seed, which no clone has done on every seed, and below the teacher's 0.746; clone against the champion ci-69, a clone of search-4, above one half on every seed for the first time if the edge carries through cloning, and the gate then names it committable (this run does not commit: commit is a dispatch field). The value policy is a different fit on a different distribution and its rows cannot be read against ci-106's; its mean row, if the mean step is on this branch by then, is read against ci-106's 0.48 and 0.4625 as one sample. What would refute the idea: a clone at parity with search-4 again, which would say the clone caps below its teacher rather than at it, and the teacher's edge over search-4 is in decisions the clone's linear model cannot copy. The cost is ci-106's, about an hour and twenty minutes.
